question: Does SV pick better stocks than chance? Every SV signal is copied with a random stock from the same universe that traded that day, bought and sold by the same rules; SV's account is ranked against 200 such random accounts, and its trades against random trades bought the same day.
next_step: If selection skill is shown: E2, SV fills the 25% stock slice of the core with SPY filling the gaps. If not: SV's stock picks are not built on; research turns to SV's market and sector reading (graded exposure, sector-fund rotation) and to finding why the picks fail.
notes: Pre-registered success (both must hold): SV's account Sharpe beats at least 95% of the 200 random accounts, and SV's trades return more than random trades bought the same day with a t value of at least 2 (signal months as clusters).

Random picks: same signal days and same-day order as SV, a random stock from the 1,223-stock universe with a bar that day and a year of history, the same next-open entry, its own support stop from bars up to the signal day, no 2R target and a 40-day exit; same account (5% per stock, up to 10, risk 0.5%, open risk 10%).
Both sides share the universe's survivorship and selection biases, so the comparison isolates which stock was chosen.
Style check (reported, not a pass condition): the same share of the account in SPY, QQQ, IWM or RSP on the same days, and SV's daily returns regressed on SPY, QQQ minus SPY and IWM minus SPY.
Same window and settings as step 1 (2005-09-12 to 2026-01-16), so SV's own account reproduces step 1's carried-forward result.
